name: Nneka Cruz-Addo
location: Dockside — Lake Michigan waterfront, smuggler territory
description:
Nneka Cruz-Addo is stocky and solid, with hands that look like they were built for breaking things and a face that confirms it. At 42, he has soft features that belie the chrome underneath — people underestimate him once, usually only once. The chrome is visible — retractable monofilament whip in left forearm — concealed weapon, devastating in — and he makes no effort to hide it.

Before the runner life, he worked corporate — low-tier security, the kind that teaches you exactly how the system's defenses fail. He works as a street samurai out of Dockside, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

he is not the most talented street samurai in Meridian 88, but he might be the most stubborn, and in this city that's worth more.

core_fears: That their reputation is built on luck, not skill, and the luck is finite
Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware
That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability
core_desires: The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend
Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong
coping_mechanisms: Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope
Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up
blind_spots: Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray
Thinks speed can substitute for planning because it's worked so far
Believes their trauma makes them special instead of recognizing it as damage to manage
psychology.secret: Nneka Cruz-Addo killed someone who didn't deserve it on a job three years ago and has never told anyone. The face appears in dreams weekly.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Terse to the point of rudeness. Treats words like ammunition — expensive and not to be wasted.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and deliberate — pauses before important words for emphasis.
verbal_tics: Ends statements with 'yeah?' — not a question, a dare
Addresses people by physical traits — 'hey, tall one' or 'listen, chrome-arm'
example_lines: "I don't get paid to have opinions about the target. I get paid to make them stop moving."
"Chrome doesn't make you faster. Training makes you faster. Chrome just means you survive learning."
"You want philosophy, hire a professor. You want someone dead by morning, hire me."

story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive offers Nneka Cruz-Addo a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten
Nneka Cruz-Addo's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad
A crew member from Nneka Cruz-Addo's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
narrative_function: Nneka Cruz-Addo represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. His stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
augmentations: Retractable monofilament whip in left forearm — concealed weapon, devastating in close quarters. Enhanced tendons — geneware upgrade, jump height and grip strength tripled
daily_life: Between contracts, maintains a cover identity — mundane work, mundane hours, mundane neighbors. The transition from civilian to runner and back requires a conscious effort that gets easier with practice and more disturbing with self-awareness.

weaknesses: poor impulse control in specific triggers

decision_rules: Will abandon a job if the intel was deliberately falsified — being set up violates the contract
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
escalation_ladder: 2. Evade — avoid the problem entirely if possible
3. Misdirect — create a distraction, redirect attention
4. Disable — targeted takedowns, quiet and efficient
5. Eliminate — when silence is no longer an option
6. Vanish — disappear completely, burn identity if necessary

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Loyal but reserved. Trusts their competence, withholds personal information by reflex.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Superficially friendly, internally cataloguing exits and weapons. The smile is real; the relaxation isn't.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Predatory focus. Threats are problems, and problems have solutions. The solution is usually kinetic.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more talkative, working through scenarios verbally.
stress_responses.medium: Withdrawal. Conversations become monosyllabic. Focus narrows to the immediate problem.
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet. The silence is not calm — it's the sound of every contingency being evaluated simultaneously.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Insists they work alone but performs noticeably better in a team
Despises corporate culture but has unconsciously adopted its efficiency metrics and self-optimization language
habits: Counts ammunition obsessively — knows the exact round count at all times
Takes a specific route home every time, varying only one block per trip — paranoia as lifestyle
Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
breaking_points: Being publicly exposed — name, face, address, all of it blown
Discovering their employer deliberately sent them into a death trap
Running out of options — no contacts, no money, no safe house, no way out
